players.product: electronic specialty and bulk gases (Taiyo Nippon Sanso, Nippon Sanso Matheson)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Kubo: for the first quarter (April-June 2026) revenue was JPY 361.7 billion, up 14.9% year on year (up 5.9% excluding foreign exchange; FX contributed 8.6%), helped by price management, a modest volume / mix contribution and acquired businesses mainly in Europe and Oceania. Core operating profit was JPY 54.6 billion, up JPY 9.0 billion or 19.9% (9.8% excluding FX); core operating margin rose from 14.5% to 15.1% and EBITDA margin improved 120 basis points to 25.0%. Net non-recurring gains of JPY 10.0 billion, mainly a gain on the sale of headquarters land.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue JPY 361.7 billion (+14.9%); core operating profit JPY 54.6 billion (+19.9%); core operating margin 15.1%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Watanabe: demand for data-center servers keeps expanding on generative AI; the semiconductor market remains robust, particularly in memory, chipmakers are generally running at high utilization and capital investment, especially in leading-edge technologies, stays strong - a tailwind for the electronics business. CFO Kubo: shipments of electronic materials gases continued to perform solidly, particularly in Asia, on strong AI and data-center related demand. Management: electronics growth in Asia and Japan in Q1 was driven primarily by higher volumes; electronic materials gases compete in global markets and are priced product by product. In Asia-Oceania the electronics business performed better than expected, with South Korea significantly better than originally expected and China and Taiwan largely in line.

CEO Watanabe: Q1 capital expenditures totaled JPY 28.5 billion, up year on year. The capital expenditure backlog (projects of about JPY 500 million or more) stood at approximately JPY 150 billion at the end of June 2026 versus approximately JPY 180 billion a quarter earlier, mainly because existing projects progressed and completed - including the hydrogen supply project for the Numaligarh Refinery in India - more than offsetting newly added projects. CFO Kubo: the Nippon Ekitan project is in the backlog's 'Others' category; the Shunan Sanso project is not yet included, will be reflected from the second quarter, and is smaller than the Nippon Ekitan project (amount not disclosed).
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 capex JPY 28.5 billion; capex backlog approximately JPY 150 billion (from approximately JPY 180 billion)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 segments (CFO Kubo): Japan revenue JPY 96.7 billion (-0.7%) and segment profit JPY 12.0 billion (-9.7%), mainly on lower electronics-related equipment and engineering revenue while price management and electronic materials gas sales stayed solid; United States revenue JPY 99.1 billion (+18.0%) and profit JPY 14.9 billion (+30.8%) on higher gas volumes, pricing and higher equipment sales for industrial gas and electronics; Europe revenue JPY 97.8 billion (+18.8%) and profit JPY 18.9 billion (+18.4%) despite lower gas volumes; Asia-Oceania revenue JPY 58.8 billion (+39.2%) and profit JPY 7.1 billion (+106.9%) on the Oceania acquisition and higher electronic materials gas volumes; Thermos revenue JPY 9.1 billion (+5.5%) and profit JPY 1.8 billion (+10.3%). Operating cash flow JPY 54.7 billion (+31.3%); free cash flow JPY 38.2 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: US profit JPY 14.9 billion (+30.8%); Asia-Oceania profit JPY 7.1 billion (+106.9%); Japan profit JPY 12.0 billion (-9.7%)

quarterly_data.signal: Equipment and engineering (CEO Watanabe): Japan equipment and engineering revenue fell because the prior year included several large projects, but the number of new project opportunities is increasing; in the U.S. the electronics gas business is performing particularly well (demand driven by the global semiconductor market) and the equipment pickup is in equipment for silicon semiconductor (memory and logic) manufacturing, not MOCVD - MOCVD-related order intake in the U.S. is broadly unchanged. Management sees no significant change in the competitive environment for semiconductor-fab projects; in Japan the industry's capacity to execute such projects is constrained to some extent by resources and manpower.

Outlook (management): Q1 Asia-Oceania and the United States performed better than anticipated and Europe largely in line. CFO Kubo expects Q2 to progress broadly in line with plan, at about the Q1 level with potential for modest volume growth; no material Q2 projects were pulled into Q1, large equipment and engineering projects often contribute in Q4, and on-site volumes are beginning to recover in some regions (Europe on-site volumes on a gradual recovery path from Q2; European volumes slightly down as customers turn cautious on Strait of Hormuz and Ukraine uncertainty). U.S. volume growth is driven mainly by bulk and on-site, with packaged gas weaker. Helium: the price increase is progressing steadily; with limited exposure to Qatar the Middle East situation did not significantly affect the helium business in Q1. Higher electricity prices had minimal impact on Japan in Q1, with pass-through subject to a time lag. In Europe the company made an additional investment in Italian engineering company HYSYTECH and acquired a majority stake.
